abstractions: Two pages, two queued writes and four non-reused draft revisions represent source limits of 20 pages and arbitrary UUID revisions.
Opaque image identities encode already-validated MIME, dimensions and size. Each text layer stays with its image through reorder and is cleared on image replacement.

The exported flag follows the source UI retry lock and does not assert that a provider has saved a PDF. Requested, unverified and unconfirmed outcomes lock retry; failed, unavailable, too-large and cancelled do not, on either route.

Text recognition and page correction run under the document's busy flag and are atomic; the searchable review is modeled from its Download step. A searchable review closed after its provider request settles the picker flag at once.
Autosave marks only a draft it created. An explicit save or a load clears the mark, so a confirmed export leaves that draft, and removing the last page deletes only a draft this review created.
One representative note with opaque contents, three revisions and a three-step Trash age. A full Trash is an environment flag; the refusal remembers the refused revision.
Confirmed Empty Trash, Delete forever and the full-Trash permanent deletion are the only ways a deleted note younger than the retention period has no Trash row.
The kept draft is one flag here; its merge, apply and clear rules are in NotesDraftSlot, and the Trash surface is in NotesTrashSession.

The domain starts present or absent, with or without legacy bytes. Creation by the first read keeps version 0; a concurrent creator is a concurrent write.
Encryption and storage-engine transactional correctness are environment contracts.
Finite representative identities and contents for one file-to-email review. A failed insert leaves only Cancel until the review is opened again.

abstractions: Three representative entries (two files and one created folder), two folder identities, two sessions, revisions 0..2 and up to four applied effects.
Opaque entry and selection capabilities retain their role without provider paths or credentials. Tree access and separately selected document access remain distinct.

Provider failures and stale revisions are per-item; a committed item is not rolled back when a later item fails. Review is required before mutation; the delete review states permanence and native requires confirmPermanent.
Share and save hand rows to Android without changing the tree. The recent list and its grants are in FilesRecentIndex.
The model covers Alpha tree orchestration and native request admission. Document provider filesystem implementation and exact payload bytes remain implementation test boundaries.
One operation, two owner identities, two source revisions and open/expired/clock-changed windows.
Atomic durable writes are represented by storage success; capacity and multi-row scheduling are omitted.
A stored dispatching row projects unknown on restart and is never automatically dispatched again.

A changed owner or source pauses the row before any dispatch, and Undo of an undone row returns it again. The browser reminder twin is held to the same rules; the Calendar twin is allocated to CalendarSync.
One permitted item and one app-owned capture identity, two source revisions, five library epochs, four selection tickets and up to three owned rows.
Full/selected summarize permitted access; mixed/partial policies are represented by current per-item permission. Lock is the locked scope Android reports, which ends the permitted catalog only.

Photo, video and assistant captures are saved by the shutter with no review; scan mode holds one unsaved frame whose keep commit is not fenced, so a review closed meanwhile leaves a committed photo with an unshown outcome.

A hidden page clears the permitted catalog only when the library is readable, finishes a recording, and keeps the scan frame only when a system picker was open. The 120-second review lifetime is two ticks.

Exact content/hash equality is represented by matching revision identities; codecs and pixel transforms are omitted. Preview, recording, copy receipts and the device library are detailed in CameraPreview, VideoRecorder, CopyReceipt and DeviceLibrary.
